newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mixed, late soybean rally cited.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mixed, late soybean rally cited.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed with the market buoyed late by a rally in soybean futures, traders said.
The market was pressured early on a setback tied to signals the market was technically overbought, traders said.

Position squaring was featured ahead of the weekend and before the release late Friday of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report. That report is expected to confirm trade thinking of a recent large buildup of fund long positions, a scenario that slowed bullish momentum in the market late this week.
Also resistance near the $3.00 per bushel level helped steer new longs away from the market in early dealings Friday, the traders said.

The posting Friday of no delivery notices against the March contract was taken in stride by the market because it wasn't expecting any deliveries. Friday was first notice day for deliveries against the CBOT March contracts.
Corn closed one cent per bushel higher to 1/2 lower, with March up 3/4 at $2.96-3/4. May was unchanged at $2.95-1/4.

News private exporters reported the sale of 101,600 tonnes of U.S. corn to Japan failed to generate new buying but commercial bull spreading helped limit declines. Continental Grain did four million bushels of March/May, traders said.
ADM Investor Services was a net buyer of 4.5 million bushels of July and Cargill Inc was an outright buyer of 4.0 million bushels of May, traders said.
Refco Inc, R.J. O'Brien and Farmers Commodities Corp each sold one million bushels of May, traders said.
Technicians early Friday reported first support in the May at $2.92 and second support at $2.85-1/2. The session low for May was $2.92-1/4.
First resistance was at $2.98 and second resistance was at $3.04-1/2. The session high was $2.95-1/2.
The four and 20-day moving averages showed bullish signals early Friday.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for the March closed at 82 percent. The market views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 85,000 contracts, below the 115,197 traded Thursday.

In corn options, LIT America sold 500 May $2.80 puts at 4-1/2 cents, FIMAT Futures bought 500 May $2.80 calls at 18-1/4 cents and ADM Investor Services sold 500 May $2.90 calls at 11-7/8 to 12-1/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 24,000 contracts, up from the 23,477 traded Thursday.
